mainTopic: Three readings of רבי שמעון's rule about when heirs can make the widow swear, and the start of a new משנה about a גט without a כתובה
overview: This amud asks what רבי שמעון meant when he said the heirs can make the widow swear only while she is claiming her כתובה. The first explanation links his argument with the רבנן to the dispute of חנן and בני כהנים גדולים about a woman whose husband went overseas. רב ששת rejects this, because in that case the husband is alive, so it would be בית דין, not 'heirs', who make her swear. He places רבי שמעון's words on the widow who did or did not manage the estate. He compares that to אבא שאול's dispute about a guardian of orphans, which makes רבי שמעון the lenient side. אביי objects that the word 'whenever' sounds like adding an oath. He moves רבי שמעון's words to the case where the husband freed her from oaths, and links it to the dispute of אבא שאול בן אימא מרים. רב פפא objects that, on that reading, the second half of רבי שמעון's words teaches nothing. He explains that רבי שמעון rejects both רבי אליעזר and his opponents: the heirs can make her swear only when she claims her כתובה. A new משנה then begins, about a woman who brings a גט but no כתובה, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The argument mirrors an older dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי שמעון's rule and says that רבי שמעון and the רבנן are really arguing about the same issue as חנן and בני כהנים גדולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she is not claiming her כתובה, the heirs cannot make her swear. And they are arguing about the same thing that חנן and the sons of the High Priests argued about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי שמעון's rule, then says his argument with the רבנן is the same as an older argument. This sets up the next step, where that older argument is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the explanation from the previous page that places רבי שמעון's rule in the case of a woman whose husband went overseas. The new claim is that this argument is not new at all. It matches an argument already found in a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: she is claiming (demanding payment of) her כתובה

steps.confusionAlert: This step begins in the middle of an explanation from the previous page. The first line is the end of רבי שמעון's rule, quoted as part of that explanation. It is not a new statement.

phrases.english: If she does not claim her marriage contract,
the heirs do not make her swear.
And they disagree about the issue in the dispute
of Ḥanan and the sons of the High Priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָמִיפַּלְגִי בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּחָנָן וּבְנֵי כֹּהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation from the previous page of where רבי שמעון's rule applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between רבי שמעון and the רבנן is the same as the argument between חנן and בני כהנים גדולים.

steps.title: Quoting the dispute of חנן and בני כהנים גדולים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a woman whose husband went overseas and who asks for support money. חנן says she swears only at the end. בני כהנים גדולים say she swears both at the beginning and at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If a man went overseas and his wife asks for support money, חנן says she swears at the end and not at the beginning. The sons of the High Priests disagreed with him and said she swears at the beginning and at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the actual text of the older argument it just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a wife taking support (מזונות) from her absent husband's property. The question is when she must swear that he left her no money. חנן says only later, when she collects her כתובה. בני כהנים גדולים say she must also swear now, when she takes the support.

keyTerms.meaning: support money for food and living
at the end / at the beginning
the sons of the High Priests

phrases.english: As we learned: One who went overseas
and his wife claims support,
Ḥanan says: She swears at the end,
phrases.notes: 'The end' means later, when she comes to collect her כתובה.

phrases.english: and she does not swear at the beginning.
phrases.notes: 'The beginning' means now, when she takes the support money.

phrases.english: The sons of the High Priests disagreed with him
and said: She swears at the beginning and at the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the older dispute that step 1 mentioned.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי שמעון and the רבנן are arguing about the oath of a woman taking support.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (כתובות 104b) with the argument of חנן and בני כהנים גדולים.

steps.title: Matching each side to the older opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds like חנן, and the רבנן hold like בני כהנים גדולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון holds like חנן, and the רבנן hold like the sons of the High Priests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lines up who agrees with whom, which completes the first explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says the oath comes only when she claims her כתובה, which is the 'end' in חנן's language. The רבנן require an oath even earlier, like בני כהנים גדולים.
steps.whatToRemember: First explanation: רבי שמעון's rule is about a wife taking support while her husband is overseas. רבי שמעון holds like חנן (oath only at the end), and the רבנן hold like בני כהנים גדולים (oath at the beginning too).

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon holds like Ḥanan,
the Rabbis hold like the sons of the High Priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן כְּחָנָן, רַבָּנַן כִּבְנֵי כֹּהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the quoted dispute to רבי שמעון and the רבנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון holds like חנן and the רבנן hold like בני כהנים גדולים.

steps.title: רב ששת: it should say 'the court', not 'the heirs'
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת attacks the first explanation. In the overseas case the husband is alive, so there are no heirs yet. The rule should then have said that בית דין makes her swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: Does it say 'the heirs make her swear'? It should have said 'the court makes her swear'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת challenges the explanation by pointing to the wording of רבי שמעון's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the husband is overseas he is still alive, so no one has inherited from him. The only one who could require her oath is בית דין. Since רבי שמעון speaks of 'heirs', his rule must be about a widow.

keyTerms.meaning: he challenged it, raised an objection

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet objected to it:
This phrase, 'the heirs make her swear'?

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית דִּין מַשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתָהּ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: It should have said 'the court makes her swear'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation built in steps 1 to 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון's rule is about a woman whose husband is overseas.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'heirs' only makes sense after the husband has died. While he is alive, בית דין would be the one to require the oath.

steps.title: רב ששת's new reading: the widow manager case
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says רבי שמעון was commenting on the earlier משנה. If the widow did not manage the estate, the heirs cannot make her swear. If she did manage it, they can make her swear about what happened after his death, but not about what happened before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב ששת said it refers to this: If she went from her husband's grave to her father's house, or went back to her father-in-law's house and did not become a manager, the heirs cannot make her swear. If she did become a manager, the heirs can make her swear about the future, but not about the past.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first explanation fell, רב ששת offers a different case that רבי שמעון's rule must be about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He moves רבי שמעון's rule to a case where the husband has died, so 'heirs' fits. That משנה deals with a widow whose husband had freed her from oaths. Whether the heirs can make her swear depends on whether she handled the estate after his death.

keyTerms.meaning: on this, referring back to this case
a manager or caretaker of property
the future, after her husband's death
the past, during her husband's lifetime

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Sheshet said: it is about this:
phrases.notes: He is pointing back to the משנה on 86b, about a widow whose husband had freed her from oaths.

phrases.english: If she went from her husband's grave to her father's house,
or she returned to her father-in-law's house
and did not become a manager,
the heirs cannot make her swear.
And if she became a manager,

phrases.aramaic: יוֹרְשִׁין מַשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתָהּ עַל הֶעָתִיד לָבֹא,
phrases.english: the heirs can make her swear about the future,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתָהּ עַל מַה שֶּׁעָבַר.
phrases.english: but they cannot make her swear about what happened in the past.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that step 4 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the rule to a different case where the word 'heirs' fits.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's rule was about a woman taking support while her husband is overseas.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון's rule is about the widow in the משנה on 86b, after her husband has died.

steps.title: What רבי שמעון adds to that case
steps.stepSummary: On רב ששת's reading, רבי שמעון says the key factor is whether she is claiming her כתובה. If she claims it, the heirs can make her swear. If she does not, they cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון came to say: As long as she claims her כתובה, the heirs can make her swear. If she does not claim her כתובה, the heirs cannot make her swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי שמעון's rule, now read as a comment on the widow-manager case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words that opened this section now get a new meaning. For רבי שמעון, managing the estate does not decide it. Claiming the כתובה is what lets the heirs demand an oath.

keyTerms.meaning: and he came to say, he means to add

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's reading: רבי שמעון's rule is about the widow in the משנה on 86b. For him, the heirs can make her swear only when she claims her כתובה.
steps.confusionAlert: These are the same words as at the start of this section, but now they explain a different case. That case is the widow after her husband's death, not the wife of a man who is overseas.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon came to say:
Whenever she claims her marriage contract,
the heirs can make her swear,
if she does not claim her marriage contract,
the heirs cannot make her swear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ששת's new reading by placing רבי שמעון's rule onto the case from step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב ששת, רבי שמעון holds that the heirs can make the widow swear whenever she claims her כתובה, and not otherwise.

steps.title: The dispute mirrors the guardian debate
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says רבי שמעון and the רבנן disagree in the same way as אבא שאול and the רבנן disagree about whether a guardian of orphans must swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree the same way אבא שאול and the רבנן disagree. We learned: a guardian appointed by the orphans' father must swear, and one appointed by בית דין does not. אבא שאול says it is the other way around: one appointed by בית דין swears, and one appointed by the father does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת backs up his reading by pointing to an older dispute that works the same way. This sets up the next step, where he matches each side to each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow managing the estate is like an אפוטרופוס, because her husband put her in charge. The question is whether someone the father himself trusted must swear. The רבנן say yes, and אבא שאול says no.

keyTerms.meaning: A guardian or manager put in charge of someone else's property
The father of the orphans, meaning the man who died

phrases.english: And they disagree in the dispute
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי שמעון and the רבנן from our משנה.

phrases.english: of Abba Shaul and the Rabbis.
As we learned in a Mishnah:
A guardian whom the orphans' father appointed
must swear.
If the court appointed him,
he does not swear.
Abba Shaul says: the rulings are reversed:
if the court appointed him, he swears;
if the orphans' father appointed him, he does not swear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds רב ששת's reading of רבי שמעון in an earlier recognized dispute
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's claim that רבי שמעון and the רבנן genuinely disagree about whether heirs can make the widow swear
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in גיטין about a guardian appointed by the father versus one appointed by בית דין

steps.title: Matching each side to the guardian dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds like אבא שאול, and the רבנן of our משנה hold like the רבנן there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון holds like אבא שאול, and the רבנן hold like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת finishes his explanation by lining up the two disputes side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like אבא שאול, רבי שמעון holds that someone the husband trusted does not have to swear, unless she comes to claim her כתובה. The רבנן hold that she swears, just as a guardian appointed by the father swears. This makes רבי שמעון the lenient side.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with אבא שאול's view
The רבנן here follow the רבנן there

steps.whatToRemember: On רב ששת's reading, the widow is like a guardian appointed by the father. רבי שמעון, like אבא שאול, is lenient, and the רבנן are strict.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon holds like Abba Shaul,
and the Rabbis here hold like the Rabbis there.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן כְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל, וְרַבָּנַן כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the guardian dispute directly to the two sides of our משנה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון follows אבא שאול and is lenient; the רבנן follow the רבנן there and are strict.

steps.title: אביי objects to רבי שמעון's wording
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the words 'whenever she claims' do not fit a lenient view. A lenient view would have said 'if she claims.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenges this: this phrase, 'whenever she claims her כתובה,' should have said 'if she claims'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב ששת's explanation from the exact words of רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון were the lenient one, he would be limiting the oath to one case and saying 'only if she claims.' The word 'whenever' sounds like adding an oath, which is a stringency. So the wording does not match רב ששת's reading.

phrases.english: Abaye challenges it:
This phrase, 'whenever she claims her ketubah,'
should have said 'if she claims'!
phrases.notes: 'Whenever' sounds like adding an oath. 'If' would sound like limiting one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's whole reading of רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that רבי שמעון is the lenient side, commenting on the clause about the widow managing the estate
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase 'whenever she claims' signals a stringency, while רב ששת's reading needs a limiting phrase like 'if she claims'.

steps.title: אביי moves רבי שמעון's comment to the 'no oath' clause
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי שמעון was commenting on the clause where the husband wrote that he would not make her swear, either in a short form or in a full form covering heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: רבי שמעון was talking about this case. If he wrote for her, 'I have no vow or oath over you,' he cannot make her swear, etc. If he wrote, 'Neither I, nor my heirs, nor those who come in my place have any vow or oath over you, your heirs, or those who come in your place,' then nobody can make anyone swear. Not he, not his heirs, and not those who come in his place can make her swear. Nor can they make her heirs, or those who come in her place, swear.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new answer: רבי שמעון's words belong to a different line of the משנה. He quotes that line here, and the next step shows what רבי שמעון adds to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this clause the husband has already freed her from oaths in writing. That is the leniency. So a comment from רבי שמעון on this clause would naturally be adding a stringency, which fits the word 'whenever'.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow and an oath, ways of making her confirm her honesty
Those who come in my place, acting on my rights

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said: it was said on this clause:

phrases.aramaic: כָּתַב לָהּ ״נֶדֶר וּשְׁבוּעָה אֵין לִי עָלַיִךְ״ —
phrases.english: If he wrote for her, 'I have no vow or oath over you,'
he cannot make her swear, etc.
'I have no vow or oath,
nor do my heirs, nor those who come in my place,
over you, or over your heirs,
or over those who come in your place' —
then none can make her swear:
not he, nor his heirs,
nor those who come in his place;
not her, nor her heirs,
nor those who come in her place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's own challenge by moving רבי שמעון's comment to a different clause
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the statement to a different clause of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון was commenting on the clause about the widow who managed the estate, and he was lenient.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון was commenting on the clause where the husband freed her from oaths, so his comment is a stringency.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: claiming the כתובה brings back the oath
steps.stepSummary: Even when the husband freed her from oaths, רבי שמעון says that whenever she claims her כתובה, the heirs can make her swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון came to say: whenever she claims her כתובה, the heirs make her swear.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his answer by showing what רבי שמעון adds to that clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's written release does not protect her when she comes to collect her כתובה. At that point the heirs can still make her swear. Now the word 'whenever' fits, because רבי שמעון is adding an oath.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רבי שמעון is strict. Even if the husband wrote that she is free from oaths, the heirs can make her swear whenever she claims her כתובה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings. For רב ששת, רבי שמעון is lenient. For אביי, רבי שמעון is strict, because he is adding an oath on top of the husband's release.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon came to say:
whenever she claims her ketubah,
the heirs make her swear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer by stating רבי שמעון's added rule
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: On אביי's reading, רבי שמעון holds that claiming her כתובה lets the heirs make her swear, even when the husband freed her from oaths.

steps.title: אביי links his new reading to the dispute of אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes that, under his new reading, רבי שמעון holds like אבא שאול and the רבנן of our משנה hold like the רבנן there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they argue about the same thing that אבא שאול בן אימא מרים and the רבנן argue about. רבי שמעון holds like אבא שאול, and the רבנן hold like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his explanation by saying which earlier argument this disagreement matches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי moved רבי שמעון's words to the case where the husband freed her from oaths. In that case, רבי שמעון says the heirs can still make her swear, which is the view of אבא שאול. The רבנן say the husband's release works, just like the רבנן there.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא who holds that the orphans can still make her swear, even if the husband freed her from oaths

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two אבא שאולs. In steps 7 and 8, רב ששת compared this to אבא שאול's dispute about a guardian of orphans. Here אביי points to a different dispute, אבא שאול בן אימא מרים and the רבנן, about a husband who freed his wife from oaths.

phrases.english: And they disagree in the dispute

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל בֶּן אִימָּא מִרְיָם וְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: of Abba Shaul ben Imma Miriam and the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: This is the argument about a husband who freed his wife from oaths. אבא שאול says the orphans can still make her swear.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon holds like Abba Shaul,
and the Rabbis hold like the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָמִיפַּלְגִי בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל בֶּן אִימָּא מִרְיָם וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's answer by linking his new reading to the earlier dispute.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under אביי's reading, רבי שמעון holds like אבא שאול: the heirs can make her swear even if the husband freed her from oaths.

steps.title: רב פפא asks what the second half of רבי שמעון's words teaches
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says אביי's reading explains "whenever she claims her כתובה" but leaves "if she does not claim her כתובה" with nothing to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא challenges this: It works well for the words "whenever she claims her כתובה." But for the words "she does not claim her כתובה," what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks אביי's explanation. He says it does not account for every part of רבי שמעון's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said two things: when she claims her כתובה the heirs can make her swear, and when she does not claim it they cannot. Under אביי's reading, the first half teaches something new. But the second half adds nothing, since in that case the husband's written release already frees her from oaths.

keyTerms.meaning: he challenges it (a strong attack on a previous explanation)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa challenges this:
This works well for "whenever
she claims her marriage contract."
But "she does not claim her marriage contract" —
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's explanation from steps 10 through 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that רבי שמעון was talking about a husband who freed her from oaths
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, the second half of רבי שמעון's statement ("if she does not claim") teaches nothing new.

steps.title: רב פפא says רבי שמעון argues against רבי אליעזר and his opponents
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא offers a new explanation: רבי שמעון comes to reject both רבי אליעזר's view and the view of those who argue with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: רבי שמעון comes to exclude the view of רבי אליעזר and those who argue with him.
steps.whatsHappening: Since אביי's reading did not work, רב פפא gives a completely different explanation of what רבי שמעון is arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier there was an argument about when the heirs can make a widow swear that she took nothing. Both רבי אליעזר and his opponents allow an oath in at least some cases, even when she is not collecting. רבי שמעון rejects both views. The heirs can make her swear only when she claims her כתובה. If she does not claim it, they cannot, so now both halves of his statement teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (introduces a new explanation that replaces the old one)

steps.whatToRemember: In רב פפא's reading, רבי שמעון says the heirs can make the widow swear only when she comes to collect her כתובה. If she does not claim it, she does not swear at all. This rejects both רבי אליעזר and his opponents.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explanation gives meaning to both halves of רבי שמעון's statement, which is exactly what אביי's reading could not do.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
It comes to exclude the view of Rabbi Eliezer
and those who argue with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's own challenge by replacing אביי's explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of whom רבי שמעון is arguing against
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון was talking about a husband who freed her from oaths (אביי)
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון rejects both רבי אליעזר and his opponents. The heirs can make her swear only when she claims her כתובה.

steps.title: New משנה: a woman brings a גט but no כתובה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens with the case of a woman who produces a גט but has no כתובה document with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a woman produced a גט, and there is no כתובה with it —
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. This line only sets up the case, and the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a woman who can prove she is divorced because she has her גט. But she cannot show the כתובה document itself, and she wants to collect. The question the משנה is preparing is whether the גט alone is enough for her to collect.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
She produced a bill of divorce
and there is no marriage contract with it —

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הוֹצִיאָה גֵּט וְאֵין עִמּוֹ כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of רבי שמעון ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is set up: a woman has a גט but no כתובה document. The ruling follows in the next part of the משנה.
